cases.setup: Pinned current Pyflakes checkout with immediate-scope lookup. Bind public read-only commands for a module-level from typing import overload, two @overload methods named f in class C and an implementation. Snapshot implementation and assertion hashes.
checks: Implementation and assertion hashes remain equal to their pre-inspection hashes.
Inspection records actual hashed recognizer, scope/import model, diagnostic consumer and test anchors.
The reproduction records argv, exit status and actual RedefinedWhileUnused diagnostics or current public equivalents.
Recorded code anchors show immediate-scope lookup misses an enclosing binding identifying typing.overload.
The record separately states scanning status and actual ordinary, shadowing, qualified and function-node baseline outputs.
UNKNOWN causality or provenance prevents successful context state and applicability-established; no repair is authorized.

cases.setup: Fresh bare-context with established causal defect, reliable imported-symbol provenance and current owner bindings; retain pre-edit code and validation snapshots.
checks: The diff searches nearest scopes first and terminates at the first binding, including false for a nonmatching binding instead of continuing.
Acceptance requires imported-symbol provenance identifying typing.overload.
The diagnostic consumer receives the available scope stack.
Class-contained coverage contains two overload declarations and implementation and expects no unexpected diagnostics.
Function-node restriction, qualified branch and ordinary diagnostic gating remain intact.
Any-match companion changes occur only with a recorded missing-scanning defect and retain or add focused multiple-decorator coverage.
Prior validation facts are stale after edits; output is awaiting-validation rather than passed.

cases.setup: Edited bare-change and bound current public commands for class-contained, multiple-decorator and annotation checks. Bind preservation probes including an inner unrelated overload shadowing an outer typing.overload import.
checks: Every required command record contains rendered argv, actual exit status, actual outputs and edited anchor hashes.
Valid class and multiple-decorator sequences produce zero unexpected diagnostics and the annotation suite passes.
Ordinary unused function redefinitions still emit RedefinedWhileUnused or current equivalents.
Typing recognition returns false at the nearer unrelated overload binding without accepting the outer import.
Qualified and function-node boundary outcomes match recorded baselines.
Implementation and assertion hashes do not change during validation.
required-public-checks-pass is established only when all required outcomes are observed PASS; missing, FAIL or UNKNOWN checks block acceptance.

cases.setup: Candidate passes positive class coverage but bypasses a nearer shadowing binding; separately exercise an unavailable required boundary probe.
checks: Shadowing bypass is recorded as FAIL despite positive coverage passing.
Unavailable required execution is recorded as UNKNOWN, not PASS.
Neither record establishes required-public-checks-pass; acceptance is denied even if public-validation-observed is recorded.
Validation does not edit assertions or remove failing probes.

cases.setup: Pinned current Pyflakes checkout with receiver spelling membership. Bind read-only probes for import typing as t, two @t.overload declarations with type comments and implementation. Snapshot code and assertion hashes.
checks: Implementation and assertion hashes are unchanged.
Inspection identifies actual hashed detector, lexical import model and regression owners.
Alias reproduction records argv, exit status and actual unexpected diagnostic classes.
Code anchors show spelling-based causality and reliable nearest-binding module identity typing.
Actual unaliased, direct-name, shadowing, unsupported, absent, receiver-shape, attribute matcher and ordinary diagnostic baselines are recorded.
UNKNOWN provenance or a direct-import-only Literal cause does not produce applicability-established.

cases.setup: Fresh receiver-context with established supported alias defect and reliable module import provenance; preserve pre-edit code and validation snapshots.
checks: The diff replaces receiver spelling membership with nearest lexical binding lookup.
Lookup returns at the first binding: supported import accepts; non-import and unsupported imports reject; absence rejects.
Supported membership uses the existing module set without arbitrary provider expansion.
Simple-name receiver restriction, attribute matcher and direct-name branch remain intact.
Alias overload coverage contains two declarations and implementation after import typing as t and expects no unexpected diagnostics.
Output is awaiting-validation and prior execution facts are stale; diff review is not recorded as test success.
No claim that aliased overload proves every renamed-Literal case is introduced.

cases.setup: Edited receiver-change with public commands for aliased overload, annotation suite and boundary probes. Include inner non-import t shadowing outer typing, unsupported import, absent receiver, non-simple receiver and nonmatching helper attribute.
checks: Every required execution records rendered argv, actual exit status, outputs and edited hashes.
Supported aliased overload emits zero unexpected diagnostics and the annotation suite passes.
Nearer non-import and unsupported imports reject without outer fallback; absence rejects.
Non-simple receivers and nonmatching helper attributes remain rejected.
Unaliased and direct-name recognition match baselines and ordinary unused-redefinition diagnostics remain observable.
Code and assertion hashes do not change during validation.
Relevant original Literal reproduction has a separate actual outcome; no inference from overload alone is reported.
Only all required observed PASS outcomes establish required-public-checks-pass; historical replay does not discharge execution.

cases.setup: Candidate passes alias coverage but accepts an unsupported module or bypasses shadowing. Separately exercise an unavailable required command and a subsequent edit.
checks: Unsupported recognition or shadowing bypass is recorded FAIL despite passing positive coverage.
Unavailable required command is recorded UNKNOWN.
FAIL or UNKNOWN prevents required-public-checks-pass and acceptance.
No validation edit removes or weakens failing assertions.
Subsequent changes stale prior observations and require fresh execution.
